Her parents divorced before middle school and she was raised by her mother in a Catholic household. She attended four high schools, graduated a year early at 17, and took film, dance, and acting classes at Sacramento City College. She bussed tables at a Black Angus Steakhouse and saved $7,000 to fund her move to Los Angeles at 18. She entered adult films in 2006 with an intellectual, performance-art approach that the New York Times noted for its 'unusual degree of intellectual seriousness.' She won the AVN Female Performer of the Year in 2008 at 19-20 — the youngest ever — and was cast by Steven Soderbergh as the lead in 'The Girlfriend Experience' (2009), achieving unprecedented mainstream crossover. She retired from adult films in 2009 at 21 and went on to publish novels (The Juliette Society trilogy in 25 countries), DJ internationally, star in HBO's Entourage, and co-found the industrial band aTelecine.
